summary: Register a GitHub OAuth app under your personal account or any organization you administer. The app is created immediately with no provider review — you get a Client ID and Secret right away.
requirements: A GitHub account (personal or an organization you have admin access to)
An application name using only public information (avoid internal URLs or sensitive details)
A homepage URL for your app
An authorization callback URL (you can register up to 10)

steps.text: In the upper-right corner of GitHub, click your profile picture, then Settings.
In the left sidebar, click Developer settings, then OAuth Apps.
Click "New OAuth App" (shows as "Register a new application" if you've never created one).
Fill in Application name, Homepage URL, an optional description, and the Authorization callback URL.
Optionally enable Device Flow if your app needs it, and review the "Expire user access tokens" setting (on by default).
Click "Register application" to get your Client ID and Client Secret.

blockers: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.
Only use public information when filling out the app — GitHub explicitly warns against sensitive data like internal URLs.
"Expire user access tokens" is on by default; uncheck it only if your app isn't yet updated to handle short-lived tokens.
Up to 10 callback URLs are allowed per app; each must match exactly during the OAuth flow.
For most new integrations GitHub now recommends GitHub Apps over OAuth Apps (finer-grained permissions, short-lived tokens) — worth evaluating before committing to the OAuth App path.
